encounters.title: The Reed Weir
encounters.summary: The tide road forces vessel, anchor, testimony, people, and custody into boats too small to carry every claim together.
encounters.opening_view: The punt is waiting. Tomas Wren is standing in it. Behind him, a green-lashed skiff noses through the reeds while black water drains from the inner grate and the runner road rises stone by stone. The burden marks allow six shares for the cradle and three for everything else. Tomas has not drawn a weapon. The tide has begun taking the road back.
encounters.content:
## Situation

The Reed Weir is older than its use as an escape. When the Nine Hearths passed the cauldron from one community to another, its oak runners descended this braked stone throat to the mere. Wall rings, burden marks, keeper cuts, tide notches, and grooves polished by the cradle still describe that work more clearly than any surviving charter.

Low water gives the road forty minutes. Gwyne’s black punt waits beyond the inner grate, but Tomas Wren stands in it. A second Green Lark skiff lies behind the reeds with tow lines and a folding crossbeam. Tomas has not murdered the boatman or sunk the promised craft. He has paid Sib’s nephew, put him safely ashore, and occupied the one place from which every successful theft must become a custody negotiation.

The fort arrives in pieces. Borrowed voices predict unless divided. Vane descends under articles protecting bearers and sacred water. Mael may choose ring or witness leaves over vessel; Hew may offer military necessity without ritual ownership. Ask four things: can the load reach water, who is keeper, which people and records travel, and what remains when claims outweigh boats.

## The carrying chamber

**The southwest brake.** A long oak lever controls the cradle's descent from the vault. With the brake whole, two people regulate the loaded runners while the rest guide. If the associated custody dog was torn from the floor or the brake line cut, the cradle arrives hard. Hauling lines, wedged beams, or several bodies can still stop it. Failure costs position, time, a tool, or injury before it threatens the target itself.

**The tide shelf.** A dry ledge runs above high water. The complete cradle can wait here out of sight from the outer bank, but not from anyone descending the passage. Hiding it through a missed tide preserves the artifact while conceding the prepared escape and giving pursuers time to establish claims around it.

**The keeper's stone.** Three shallow handprints face the grate: current keeper, receiving keeper, and witness. The old circuit expected custody to be transferred here. Mael's iron plate covers the latter two prints and recognizes only his emergency custodian. The founder's seal removes the plate; tools can pry it loose; a complete Barrow declaration can make it withdraw from within.

**The winding socket.** The grate rises quietly with the outer tide key, inner winding bar, or founder's seal placed in the square rose. Force bends the teeth and leaves the route open behind the crew. Cutting the chain drops the grate rather than raising it and can trap the cauldron inside.

**The tide notches.** The upper notch marks the first water that will carry a loaded boat without pinning it against stone. The lower notch marks the last water deep enough to float the cauldron safely.

**The reed road.** Outside, a raised footpath follows the channel for half a mile before splitting toward the Crooked Magpie, Mere House, and the north road. People who cannot ride in the loaded punt can move along this path, tow from shore, hide among reeds, or make for another extraction point. A split party is vulnerable but not abandoned.

## The tide in four states

Advance one state when the crew spends substantial time, loses control of the load, performs the Full Asking after low water opens, or accepts a consequence explicitly costing tide.

### Pinned water

Before the upper notch, the outgoing current remains too high. An empty boat can approach; a loaded punt is pressed sideways against the wall. The crew can prepare the cradle on the shelf, open the grate, place tow lines, negotiate custody, or send evidence ahead. Early departure requires shore lines and skilled handling. Failure pins the boat, breaks a pole, or exposes the outer party rather than capsizing the cauldron without warning.

### The black lane

The middle twenty minutes are the clean window. The current carries the loaded punt through the reeds while remaining deep enough for the six-mark cradle. A prepared boat, intact brake, and open grate make movement reliable. Pursuit becomes a contest over ropes, keeper, anchor, and witnesses rather than repeated checks to see whether the boat simply moves.

### Sucking water

During the last ten minutes mud ridges appear. Safe capacity falls by one burden mark, poles replace oars, and every halt risks grounding. The crew may transfer people to the Lark skiff, send them to the reed road, discard a bulky tool, or accept grounding at a chosen bank. A grounded boat can be reached by foot pursuit but does not damage the cauldron by itself.

### The bare road

After the lower notch, the punt cannot float the intact cradle. The old runner grooves continue through exposed mud. Twelve steady people, two draft animals, a functioning capstan line, or an ingenious equivalent can drag it to the first deep pool. Alternatively the crew can hide the target, reverse toward another exit, negotiate witnessed seizure, or wait roughly two hours for flood. Missing the window changes posture while leaving several outcomes available.

## The target as a load

Use **burden marks** only for this carrying problem.

- Cauldron and complete cradle occupy **six marks**.
- The black punt carries **nine marks** safely during the black lane and **eight** during sucking water.
- Two competent boat hands are required, one mark each.
- The named keeper occupies the remaining ordinary mark.
- An incapacitated person, bulky tool chest, cooper's handcart, or large evidence coffer occupies one mark.
- Branoc's ring, three rolled witness leaves, ordinary gear, and a compact rite kit travel on a person without another mark.

The black punt therefore carries target, two boat hands, and one keeper. It cannot also carry the whole crew, every witness, wounded allies, prisoners, tools, and rival claimants. Additional people use the reed road, Green Lark skiff, or another exit.

The Lark skiff carries four people and cannot bear the cradle alone. Lashed beside the punt, it adds hands, stability, and witness capacity without changing which craft carries the cauldron. Cooperation solves a practical problem while making Tomas's custody demand unavoidable.

The marks are disclosed earlier through kitchen chalk, Rookwalk ledgers, and the punt's draft marks. Clever crews can prepare another boat, recruit shore haulers, reduce the party at the target, or choose another exit.

## The final custodial threshold

The cauldron crosses the grate only after a keeper states their whole name, destination, and authority for the next Asking. A complete Barrow declaration carries forward. The keeper need not repeat it unless custody changes.

Possession does not replace the recorded keeper. Tomas may seize a tow line, Vane surround the boat, or Mael recover keys without gaining authority for a Full Asking. A thief who named a false destination still owes correction before the bands answer again.

At the keeper's stone, current keeper names the receiver, receiver accepts destination and authority, and a witness touches the third print. Nine soft contractions confirm a coherent transfer. A contested transfer leaves the vessel movable but ritually closed. A coerced transfer proves possession, not authority.

Thus the crew may lose the boat and preserve custody, lose custody and save testimony, or surrender the vessel to Vane under terms that bar Mael's immediate use.

## The Nine Hearth claim

At the keeper's stone, Tomas can produce the old carrying calendar: Mere, Ash, Rowan, Gorse, Reed, Stone, Bell, Road, and Lamp, each receiving the cauldron for one winter and surrendering it onward. War, inheritance, and a keeper's own house required three disinterested hearths.

The calendar records fifty-three years of Taran emergency custody and no final release. Mere, Rowan, and Bell retain complete keeper lines; Ash and Reed bring broken seals; the remaining hearths survive through memorial societies.

**Mother Eluned of the Mere House** sent the Green Larks to carry the vessel intact to Mere House under temporary Trust custody before any ruler uses it again. She will not let an urgent royal question erase communal keeping, but her claim is not a verdict: three hearths are not nine, her seniority is disputed, and the old road never anticipated anchor, Muster, and dawn oath arriving together.

## Tomas Wren's offer

Tomas shows a green cord tied in nine unequal loops, a Mere House carrying token, and a letter naming Eluned's claim. He offers the second skiff, four skilled hands, a clean route through the reeds, false pursuit signs toward the north road, and silence about the crew.

His price is a keeper declaration naming Mere House and the surviving Trust, with no Full Asking until three disinterested hearths convene. If Branoc already spoke, Tomas demands all three witness leaves travel separately and unabridged to Mere House rather than directly to Gwyne.

Four kinds of leverage can move him.

**The exact question.** It asks what Branoc commanded, not who should rule.

**The dawn clause.** Waiting for three hearths may make the answer legally useless for another generation.

**Shared custody.** Tomas can accept one current keeper, one Mere House receiver, and a three-hearth limit on every question after Branoc's first Asking.

**Branoc's consent.** If Branoc explicitly consented to publication, Tomas will not claim he protects the dead by suppressing a willing witness. He still insists the vessel go to communal custody.

If no bargain is reached, Tomas may cooperate until the party clears Dunwarren and contest custody on the reed road. He prefers a live dispute over captured or damaged sacred power. Murder of a Lark, sale to a private patron, or announced use as spoils makes him uncompromising.

## Green Lark movement

At the third bell the Larks trigger the dancer's collapse and enter by the easiest route the crew leaves open. At the first neglected asset, they take one useful thing—hooks, tide key, service key, tally cord, or unattended boat—and use it. When the cauldron moves, Mabli Quill follows the transport line while Tomas moves to the receiving end. If the crew controls both ends, the Larks shadow rather than appear through a sealed wall.

At the custodial threshold Tomas must name Eluned and the Trust. Rebuffed, the Larks seize logistics: tow lines, skiff, capstan, winding bar, an unattended ring, or the public claim itself. Their intervention creates a rival solution and a new bargain, not compulsory combat.

## Pursuit as four objectives

Track four separable objectives.

**Vessel:** cauldron and cradle preserve future Askings.

**Anchor:** Branoc's oath-ring preserves the chance to call him again and authenticates the present inquiry.

**Testimony:** three black-water leaves preserve exact exchange and may stay the dawn oath even if the vessel is recaptured.

**Keeper:** recorded custodian carries authority to transfer, correct, or permit the next use.

Ask where each objective is and who carries it. Keeping everything together simplifies coordination but exposes all stakes to one recovery. Splitting them protects partial success while creating several vulnerable routes.

- **Vane** seeks vessel and keeper. His written order is: **hold the route, take the bearers living, preserve the water, and do not strike the cradle**. If shown exact testimony or replacement defense, he may secure rather than return the cauldron.
- **Mael** seeks the vessel before Branoc speaks. After testimony exists, he prioritizes ring and leaves because bronze cannot restore the old recital's credibility.
- **Hew** seeks a defensible morning. He may permit testimony to leave if a living council replaces the Muster.
- **Green Larks** seek vessel and custody declaration. They have little reason to steal the ring after Branoc speaks except to prevent a second immediate royal question.
- **Gwyne's coalition** seeks ring and testimony first if the cauldron is lost.

At each pursuit beat, choose one objective a pursuer can reach and one fitting means: close a grate, seize a rope, challenge a keeper, isolate a witness, offer terms, block a road, or force public identification. Do not repeatedly ask whether generic guards catch the whole party.

## Captain Vane's bounded recovery

Vane's guards use barriers before weapons. At the weir they can chock runner grooves, brace the grate, seize shore lines, occupy the reed road, or shield the keeper. They will not ordinarily shoot into the loaded punt, ignite reeds, or strike the cauldron with hooked poles. A character who knows the articles can force guards to choose between standing law and Mael's override before witnesses.

Vane can accept Night of Hearing; temporary Mere House custody inside the vale; testimony leaving while he secures the vessel; or Aderyn's replacement defense compact. He cannot accept an unnamed destination, sale to a foreign buyer, casual destruction, or departure leaving no northern command. Solving the morning-after problem is stronger leverage than exposing Mael's hypocrisy.

## Other exits

### East through the Smoke Kitchens

The east channel reaches the service rise. Four capstan hands lift the cradle to kitchen level; a reinforced cooper's cart carries it through staff yard and postern. This is slow and easiest to disguise at low Heat. Workers become witnesses, helpers, potential hostages, and people endangered by recovery. Nessa can turn the yard into ordinary legitimacy and refuses passage if the crew harmed staff or leaves the vale undefended.

### North through the Rookwalk

The north channel reaches the lifting tower. Correct counterweight raises the cradle; the siege crane lowers it beyond the wall. The court, roofs, and road see the movement. The route favors witnessed seizure, ruins secrecy, and remains strongest after the tide is gone. Founder seal, Caddoc, testimony, or a nine-hearth token can make it a public claim rather than naked theft.

### Upward through chapel and court

The crew can abandon escape and carry the dispute into chapel or court. This requires Caddoc, Aderyn, Vane or Hew, founder authority, and credible testimony. It produces Night of Hearing, public Asking, or witnessed seizure. It is strongest after Branoc speaks and weakest if the crew offers no replacement defense.

### Back into the underkeep

Retreat is valid. Tide shelf, chapel crypt, counterweight gallery, and disconnected command posts can hold the target temporarily. Retreat buys a bargain, second route, or Asking while allowing factions to converge and Mael to replace tools.

## A compact extraction procedure

1. State which bands remain, whether Branoc spoke, and who is keeper.
2. Place vessel, anchor, testimony, and keeper.
3. Choose route and transport.
4. Name the first pursuer and objective using Heat, command-network state, and faction interest.
5. Present one concrete obstacle: brake, grate, load, rope, road, witness, authority, or bargain.
6. On success move to the next stage. On failure concede position, time, exposure, injury, an objective, or a custody term. Do not reset the same obstacle.
7. At the final threshold settle destination and authority.

A normal extraction takes two or three beats after the vault. Add one for split objectives, damaged routes, or several factions at the same stage.

## Failure that preserves consequence

**Cauldron recaptured, testimony escapes.** One authenticated witness leaf and two living witnesses stay renewal until noon. Mael has physical custody but cannot renew the old recital without openly suppressing hearing.

**Cauldron escapes, ring seized.** Muster is prevented and future Askings remain possible, but Branoc cannot be called again until the anchor is recovered. Existing leaves remain valid.

**Ring escapes, cauldron recaptured.** Branoc's first opportunity survives as leverage. Mael may accelerate another rite, fortify custody, or offer a bounded Asking.

**Named keeper captured.** Carriers can continue, but future Asking remains closed until custody transfers or corrects. Vane may hold the keeper as guarantor rather than ordinary prisoner.

**Boat grounds.** The target remains intact on the old carrying road. Tow, hide, bargain, split objectives, call the Larks, or reverse routes. Grounding ends secrecy, not agency.

**One band is committed.** Record the faculty lost. Continue a diminished Asking, preserve the remaining eight, and begin restoration. Delay does not itself spend bands; commitment still requires comb, water, and spoken names.

**Crew surrenders under terms.** Surrender can establish Night of Hearing, Vane's neutral security, Aderyn's compact, Mere House custody, or public noon hearing. It is total defeat only if terms restore unrestricted Muster and erase every objective.

## If Branoc has spoken

A complete Full Asking produces three black-water leaves. Ordinarily one goes to chapel witness, one to founder or opposed household bench, and one to keeper. Each preserves the entire exchange, including Branoc's questions, conditions, uncertainty, or criticism.

One authenticated leaf with two witnesses stays the dawn renewal until noon. Three leaves and Aderyn's seal require a public hearing before a replacement Compact. No leaf automatically deposes Mael or awards land. Political force comes from preventing nobles from swearing a known simplification as Branoc's command.

Branoc confirms that he ordered the great leaves barred against riders while commanding Edric to keep wicket and river stair open for the outer ward and abandon the fort if necessary to save the people. Edric preserved the first order and violated or buried the governing protections. Mael's doctrine loses its claim to be Branoc's whole command while present defense remains necessary.

If the answer occurred without willing or credible witnesses, the leaves remain ritually exact but politically vulnerable. Extraction may prioritize a living witness as strongly as bronze.

## Immediate aftermath before dawn

### Full testimony reaches the court

The old Compact cannot renew unchanged. Aderyn proposes a one-season defense covenant: Vane commands household guard, Hew chairs a living intelligence and engineering council, levies require named valley consent, wards remain with households, and cauldron custody is heard separately at noon. Mael may accept bounded command, oppose testimony, or force a naked choice between himself and the defense he claimed only he could provide.

### Testimony escapes while the vessel remains

The oath is stayed. Mael still holds the cauldron, but each attempted use occurs under scrutiny and Vane's articles. The coalition shifts to protecting witnesses, proving excavation chain, and forcing a noon hearing.

### Vessel escapes before Branoc speaks

Muster is prevented and first Asking remains available if ring and custody survive. Nobles may nevertheless renew the Compact at dawn because no contrary testimony was heard. Custodians must ask immediately at Mere House, return under safe conduct, or accept that preserving the institution let old law harden temporarily.

### Nine Hearth Trust receives the vessel

Eluned seats the bands and recognizes no permanent owner. If Tomas accepted Branoc's urgent first Asking, the Trust sends a keeper and witness to noon hearing. If not, Eluned convenes hearths and may delay for days while the Compact renews. The artifact is safer; the political opportunity may be lost.

### Vane secures the vessel

Vane closes both Mael and thieves out of immediate use, honors witness leaves, demands living defense, and places guards under Caddoc's supervision. This becomes constitutional middle ground or military seizure depending on whether Aderyn and households constrain him.

### Mael regains unrestricted custody

If no bands were spent and ring or testimony escaped, Mael recovered the object but not certainty. He can bargain, accelerate, or override Caddoc and Vane. If every objective is recovered, excavation evidence, Trust claim, and internal opposition still prevent the world from returning unchanged.

## Campaign-scale aftermath

**Who keeps a communal sacred instrument?** The Trust has oldest claim, Taran has continuous custody and infrastructure, Caddoc represents rite, Aderyn founder authority, and outer-ward coalition excluded people. Stable settlement likely divides keeping, witnessing, and authority to ask.

**What follows Branoc's command?** Edric's conduct can be judged separately from Mael's office. Land restoration, memorial correction, compensation, succession, and blame require living evidence. Branoc does not govern the present from the cauldron.

**How is the vale defended?** Hew's living council, Vane's command, valley scouts, engineers, granary keepers, and limited levies can replace the Muster. Failure to build that arrangement strengthens Mael's argument even when his rite was wrong.

**What is owed to the twelve borrowed dead?** Each answer can be recontextualized and released. Families may demand records, apology, and restoration. Caddoc's complicity is not erased by one brave act.

**Can the nine hearths be renewed?** Dead communities, disputed seals, and altered settlements make simple restoration impossible. New hearths may be admitted, old offices ended, or a different trust written. The heist can begin a campaign about building an institution worthy of the cauldron rather than finding one true owner.

## Closing the end encounter

Record five facts:

1. Which silences remain intact?
2. Did Branoc speak, and where are the leaves?
3. Who is keeper, what destination was named, and under what authority may the next Asking occur?
4. Where are vessel, ring, testimony, and keeper at dawn?
5. What living defense replaces, limits, or fails to replace Muster and Compact?

Those answers define success better than a single boat does. Measure the heist by what truth, consent, defense, and sacred power survive—and by whom they leave answering for them at dawn.

revelations.title: The feast has three doors
revelations.description: The victory feast admits masked guests, suppliers, performers, and attached households through separate checks that can be exploited or combined.

revelations.title: The kitchens open the old service road
revelations.description: The east ash passage reaches the chapel foundations, the Barrow Stair approach, and the inner side of the Reed Weir.

revelations.title: The Rookwalk crosses the wall
revelations.description: The ruined rook tower, musicians’ gallery, chapel roofs, solar balcony, and lifting tower form an exposed but connected upper route.

revelations.title: The chapel keeps the Full Asking
revelations.description: The chapel holds the complete Full Asking, the Nine-Silence Register, Branoc's rejected petition, ritual keys, and the formal latch to the underkeep.

revelations.title: The founder’s seal waits in the solar
revelations.description: Lady Aderyn keeps a seal and plans that can open old mechanisms and give the heist public authority.

revelations.title: The Barrow Stair begins below the chapel
revelations.description: Three landings test the honored name sought, the question carried, and the living custody claimed before admitting anyone to the underkeep.

revelations.title: Borrowed counsel guards the underkeep
revelations.description: Twelve tactical fragments torn from honored dead listen between the Barrow Stair and vault, predict intruders' aims, and direct living guards through separate commands.

revelations.title: The vault lies below the drowned court
revelations.description: The target stands in a chamber connected to the Barrow Stair, House of Borrowed Voices, roof lifting shaft, and tide drain.

revelations.title: The Reed Weir is the prepared carrying road
revelations.description: A low-tide culvert can take the cauldron cradle to a waiting boat if its inner grate is opened in time.

revelations.title: Wax admits paper; a witness admits a person
revelations.description: A convincing seal clears the first check, but an admitted household witness must confirm the bearer or the gate places them under observation.

revelations.title: The third bell empties the ash passage
revelations.description: For seven minutes after the final service bell, living guards leave the ash route between the kitchens and chapel foundations.

revelations.title: A whole dead person must be invited
revelations.description: The proper rite invites one honored dead person through a true personal anchor, whole name, honestly stated question, willing witnesses, and the dead person's freedom to answer or refuse.

revelations.title: Moving the cradle wakes the borrowed council
revelations.description: The cradle's first movement sends breath through twelve copper channels, waking the severed tactical voices and prompting different predictions and guard orders.

revelations.title: Vessel and cradle are one instrument
revelations.description: The nine-banded cradle holds the stored silences in relation; separating it from the bronze vessel destroys the fullness required for a true Asking.

revelations.title: Every sacred threshold demands a keeper
revelations.description: A living keeper must name themselves, a destination, and the authority for the next Asking before the cradle can cross the chapel or tide boundary intact.

revelations.title: Low water grants forty minutes
revelations.description: The extraction channel is navigable only during a short falling-tide interval, and the inner grate needs a winding bar, seal, or destructive force.

revelations.title: The fifth bell will spend nine silences
revelations.description: At the fifth bell Mael will open all nine bands and spend generations of accumulated remembrance to extract military answers from hundreds of honored dead.

revelations.title: The oath-ring can call Branoc for the first time
revelations.description: Branoc has never been summoned; the newly recovered ring from his sealed command chamber is the first true personal anchor found since his death.

revelations.title: The Green Larks move at the third bell
revelations.description: Tomas Wren’s rival crew will trigger a court distraction and exploit whichever internal route remains open.

revelations.title: The Muster keeps skill and strips purpose
revelations.description: Mael's needle trials extracted twelve narrow answers while straining but not spending three closed bands. The Great Muster escalates that abuse by opening whole bands and extracting accurate expertise from hundreds while stripping away the love, loyalty, fear, and purpose that made each dead person's knowledge meaningful.

revelations.title: At dawn the old recital becomes obligation again
revelations.description: The assembled nobles will renew Mael's emergency authority at sunrise; testimony heard before the oath can delay or prevent it, while testimony afterward confronts fresh sworn obligations.

revelations.title: Edric’s recital carries Branoc’s authority
revelations.description: House Taran's emergency authority descends from Edric Taran's claim that Branoc ordered the western gate shut, though no surviving record carries Branoc's own hand or seal.

revelations.title: Ask what Branoc commanded
revelations.description: The agreed first question is precise and non-leading: what command did Branoc give Edric Taran at the western gate? The coalition has promised to preserve the answer even if it disappoints them.

revelations.title: The stair records words, not hearts
revelations.description: The three landings test formal name, question, and custody claims and preserve their exact wording. A precise false or provisional claim can pass, but the record, later threshold, and witnesses make the discrepancy consequential.

revelations.title: Conflicting purposes divide the borrowed council
revelations.description: Each retained answer optimizes one narrow military domain without the reason that once governed it. Simultaneous objectives or routes produce incompatible orders, forcing living guard posts to pause and seek judgment.

revelations.title: A restored reason can retract a command
revelations.description: A whole name, credible record of the missing human purpose, and an opened return cock let one retained answer qualify or retract its command and cease being held apart for Mael’s use.

revelations.title: Copper lines decide where orders arrive
revelations.description: Twelve copper throats route colored verify, seize, alter, and ambush orders to six living guard posts. Maintenance collars and shutters can redirect a correct order to the wrong post or change how guards receive it.

revelations.title: Each band preserves one human faculty
revelations.description: The nine bands preserve recognition, ordered memory, judgment, affection, self-command, temporal understanding, refusal, reciprocal speech, and voluntary departure. Opening a band does not spend a generic charge; it removes that faculty from later Askings.

revelations.title: A raised band is not yet spent
revelations.description: A keyed band first rises to a visible arrest and sounds its bell. No sacred capacity is lost until the matching comb enters the water under spoken names, leaving a reversible interval for intervention, bargaining, reseating, or sabotage.

revelations.title: Four custody dogs free the cradle
revelations.description: The ritual bands hold the Full Asking together, while four separate floor dogs secure the oak cradle to its turntable. Levers, service keys, shear pins, or force can release the target for movement without diminishing the nine silences.

revelations.title: Voluntary departure restores the nine silences
revelations.description: The closed bands lend their faculties together rather than being consumed. When the invited dead person chooses to depart through an intact Band of Rest, the silences settle back into relation and remain available for future lawful Askings.

revelations.title: Black water preserves the whole exchange
revelations.description: Three witness benches receive the complete exchange in black water-script marked by every band present. Claimant, keeper, and contrary witnesses may sign or object, but alteration breaks the marks and makes abridgment visible.

revelations.title: Mismatched parts can delay the Muster
revelations.description: Band, comb, spoken names, and question must correspond. Shallow-cut rolls, resin-filled teeth, maintenance combs, jammed keys, or a contested question board create visible delay and contradiction, though they do not permanently solve custody while Mael retains the target.

revelations.title: A lost silence cannot be reforged
revelations.description: Reforging a clasp restores machinery but not the faculty consumed through it. Names, whole histories, reasons, obligations, refusals, reciprocal duties, and rest must be honored over years or generations before a committed silence can return.

revelations.title: Three authorities can buy one night
revelations.description: A chapel witness, the founder’s seal, and a military surety can invoke the Night of Hearing, seating every band and placing the cauldron in joint custody until dawn while living defense continues. The provision buys a lawful Asking but does not settle permanent ownership.

revelations.title: The Nine Hearths claim a circuit, not a throne
revelations.description: Before House Taran’s emergency custody, nine communities kept the cauldron in rotation. Mother Eluned’s surviving trust hired the Green Larks to return it to Mere House before any ruler uses it again.

revelations.title: One punt cannot carry every claimant
revelations.description: The cradle occupies six of the punt’s nine safe burden marks, leaving room only for two boat hands and one keeper unless people split to the reed road or a second craft.

revelations.title: Possession does not make a keeper
revelations.description: Taking the cradle, boat, or keys does not transfer ritual custody. The existing keeper remains recorded until a witnessed transfer, correction, yielding, death, or proven material falsehood.

revelations.title: Vane takes bearers alive and preserves the water
revelations.description: Dunwarren’s standing articles forbid fire, missiles, hooked blades, and reckless charges around cauldron water. Guards seize routes, ropes, wheels, and keepers before striking bearers or vessel.

revelations.title: One whole witness leaf stays the oath
revelations.description: A complete black-water leaf and two named witnesses postpone renewal until noon when testimony contradicts the recital on which the Gate Compact rests, even if the cauldron is recaptured.

revelations.title: Every exit chooses its witnesses
revelations.description: The Reed Weir offers the fastest private departure, the kitchen rise supports a disguised staff-yard exit, and the Rookwalk lift offers exposed speed and strong public witnessing.

clues.description: The cradle becomes immovable at chapel and tide boundaries until a living custodian makes a complete declaration.
clues.discovery: Read the runner inscription or attempt to move the target without naming custody.

clues.title: The eel chalk on the cistern wall
clues.description: Kitchen workers mark the falling tide because the drain backs into the scullery outside a forty-minute low-water interval.
clues.discovery: Interpret the chalk marks with Melly or compare them to Sib’s tide table.

clues.title: Rook-keeper’s tide messages
clues.description: Ivo sends the weir watch a brass-ring message when the channel becomes navigable and another forty minutes later when mud closes it.
clues.discovery: Intercept two ringed rooks or persuade Ivo to explain their route.

clues.title: The two tide notches
clues.description: The inner wall marks the opening and closing water levels forty minutes apart, beyond which the channel becomes mud or flood.
clues.discovery: Inspect the tide post or wait through the falling water.

clues.title: The fifth-bell war requisition
clues.description: A stolen order calls for the household memorial rolls, nine band keys, copper name combs, and the complete chained war register to be delivered below before the fifth bell.
clues.discovery: Review the requisition Gwyne obtained from a reeve's clerk.

clues.title: Mael's second-bell declaration
clues.description: Mael publicly joins the households' memorial rolls into one war register and announces that the fifth-bell Great Muster will draw a military answer from the honored dead named there.
clues.discovery: Remain for Mael's speech or obtain the herald's prepared copy.

clues.title: The full-band opening plan
clues.description: A slate beside the campaign table assigns one class of dead advisers to each band and orders all nine opened before dawn.
clues.discovery: Read the rehearsal slate or question a voice about the planned sequence.

clues.title: Branoc's recovered oath-ring
clues.description: The ring bears Branoc's private oath-name, royal wax flaw, and mortar from the newly opened command chamber; Gwyne states plainly that Branoc has never been summoned.
clues.discovery: Examine the ring, hear Efa Rill's account, and compare Gwyne's copied wax cast.

clues.title: The royal wax comparison
clues.description: Six lifetime impressions match the recovered ring's interior flaw and oath-name, satisfying the proper rite's anchor test.
clues.discovery: Compare the ring to the sealed wax casts under Caddoc's supervision.

clues.title: The missing object in the excavation inventories
clues.description: The first inventory records gold on the crowned skeleton's right hand; Mael's later copy omits it and orders the chamber sealed.
clues.discovery: Compare the two excavation packets beside Aderyn's map.

clues.title: Tomas Wren’s announced deadline
clues.description: Tomas says his crew will enter at the third bell and names the court distraction without revealing his internal route.
clues.discovery: Hear Tomas make his proposal before leaving the Magpie.

clues.title: The dancer’s false collapse
clues.description: A masked dancer carries a bitter herb packet and keeps looking toward Tomas Wren’s man in the gallery whenever the bells are mentioned.
clues.discovery: Search the dancer, notice the signals, or recognize Tomas’s promised distraction as it begins.

clues.title: The Larks’ gallery hooks
clues.description: Fresh green cord and compact climbing hooks have been hidden behind the musicians’ gallery for Tomas Wren’s crew.
clues.discovery: Search the gallery roof or catch a Lark placing the gear.

clues.title: Caddoc's twelve trial accounts
clues.description: Each needle trial prevented the nine faculties from joining, preserved one useful answer, and erased the relationship or purpose that once governed it; the register marks three bands strained but none committed.
clues.discovery: Read the restricted trial ledger and compare it to the changing memorial inscriptions.

clues.title: Answers without reasons
clues.description: Every copper mask holds a thread drawn through a closed-band inspection hole: it can state a tactic exactly but fails when asked whom it protected, loved, feared, or served.
clues.discovery: Question several voices beyond their assigned military domain.

clues.title: The scraped words beneath the bands
clues.description: Hair-fine trial needles and three worn inspection holes explain the twelve masks, while the still-seated bands and unbroken return grooves show that no whole communal silence has yet been committed.
clues.discovery: Inspect the inner faces of the strained bands or read them in the cauldron water.

clues.title: The dawn oath agenda
clues.description: Gwyne's stolen program places renewal of the Gate Compact at sunrise, immediately after the Great Muster's counsel is presented.
clues.discovery: Read the feast agenda among the briefing papers.

clues.title: The stacked renewal copies
clues.description: Each household has a prepared oath copy and a dawn speaking order; several representatives are already rehearsing the response.
clues.discovery: Inspect the clerk's table or listen to the heralds rehearse.

clues.title: Aderyn's delay annotations
clues.description: Aderyn has marked the exact succession objection by which she can delay the dawn oath if credible Branoc testimony is imminent.
clues.discovery: Read the annotated renewal text or persuade Aderyn to explain her plan.

clues.title: Edric's recital in the public compact
clues.description: The public text quotes Branoc only inside Edric Taran's later testimony and carries no surviving royal seal.
clues.discovery: Compare the renewal copies or question a jurist at the feast.

clues.title: The memorial's careful grammar
clues.description: The chapel stone says Edric 'reported the king's command' rather than recording that any witness heard Branoc give it.
clues.discovery: Read the oldest memorial layer beneath later paint.

clues.title: The unsigned first compact
clues.description: The earliest surviving compact rests on Edric's sworn account after Branoc and the outer-ward witnesses were gone.
clues.discovery: Examine the first compact with the founder's seal.

clues.title: The coalition's single vellum question
clues.description: The agreed first question asks only what command Branoc gave Edric Taran at the western gate and assumes no answer.
clues.discovery: Read the strip on Gwyne's planning table or ask her to state the commission exactly.

clues.title: The rejected petition wording
clues.description: Gwyne's petition uses the same non-leading question and promises to preserve Branoc's full response before named witnesses.
clues.discovery: Read the petition filed beneath Mael's refusal.

clues.title: Aderyn's condition of support
clues.description: Aderyn's unsent reply agrees to help only if the first question remains unchanged and the answer is not abridged to serve either faction.
clues.discovery: Find the unsent reply beneath the founder's seal or hear Aderyn quote it.

clues.title: The correction rubric beside the witness rail
clues.description: The keeper rubric instructs witnesses to preserve the exact name, first question, and custody declaration because the stair certifies spoken form, not private truth.
clues.discovery: Read Caddoc’s marginal corrections or compare the witness rail to the stair tubes.

clues.title: The founder’s correction leaf
clues.description: A founding custody form provides procedures for correcting a declaration proven false after passage, which would be unnecessary if the stair could read intention.
clues.discovery: Open the original compact packet or ask Aderyn why correction witnesses are named.

clues.title: The black-wax registers
clues.description: Hidden panels preserve exact statements and show several historically corrected custody claims; the mouths recorded them faithfully without deciding which claimant lied.
clues.discovery: Slide open a funerary panel or follow the register chains behind a stone mouth.

clues.title: Incompatible answers below one disturbance
clues.description: A single contested declaration makes one lower voice demand seizure, another demand witnessed inquiry, and a third order the likely exit held rather than entered.
clues.discovery: Create conflicting custody claims or listen through the lower speaking mouths.

clues.title: The council has no common purpose
clues.description: Moving the witness, vessel, and intruder markers toward different routes produces accurate but mutually impossible commands from the masks.
clues.discovery: Manipulate several map markers or trigger two route sensors close together.

clues.title: Hew’s arbitration slate
clues.description: A rehearsal slate orders living posts to wait for Captain Vane whenever two trial answers disagree, because Mael’s advisers cannot rank the things they propose to save.
clues.discovery: Read the guard protocol beside the war roll or compare crossed-out trial commands.

clues.title: The rubric for returning a severed answer
clues.description: A condemned keeper’s note says a retained answer may be turned back toward silence if its whole name and the human reason governing the answer are spoken together.
clues.discovery: Read beneath the pasted military amendments or ask Caddoc about the masks’ return cocks.

clues.title: Accounts preserve what the memorials lost
clues.description: Unabridged household records restore the people and promises omitted from several famous military decisions now retained as borrowed answers.
clues.discovery: Compare the old winter, bridge, compensation, and campaign accounts to public memorial copies.

clues.title: Alwen’s command retracts when her reason returns
clues.description: Speaking Alwen Reed’s ferry vow while turning her mask inward makes the retained voice refuse to strand people at the weir and then choose silence.
clues.discovery: Use a preserved reason at the matching mask and open its return cock.

clues.title: Colored shutters above the east speaking tube
clues.description: Kitchen staff distinguish white verification, red closure, blue machinery, and black waiting orders by a rotating shutter on the underkeep tube.
clues.discovery: Watch an order arrive at the east passage or ask Nessa what the four shutters mean.

clues.title: The Rook Gallery line has a maintenance collar
clues.description: The copper order line at the roof post can be detached and fitted to an adjacent collar during repairs, proving the lower switchboard is physically reroutable.
clues.discovery: Inspect the gallery speaking tube or trace its repair tags toward the underkeep.

clues.title: The six-post switchboard
clues.description: Twelve labeled copper throats terminate in removable collars and colored shutters before continuing to six living guard posts.
clues.discovery: Open the brass panel under the map table or follow a spoken command through its line.

clues.title: The nine omissions in the keeper rubric
clues.description: Caddoc’s oldest rubric names the Face, Road, Measure, Hearth, Hand, Season, Bar, Reply, and Rest as the relations required for one dead person to answer whole.
clues.discovery: Read the unpasted column beside the Full Asking instructions or persuade Caddoc to explain why the nine bands are not charges.

clues.title: The masks display different absences
clues.description: The twelve retained answers fail in distinct ways that correspond to missing recognition, sequence, judgment, affection, authorship, temporal sense, refusal, reply, or release.
clues.discovery: Compare several voices under the return procedure or inspect the nine labeled copper manifolds below the masks.

clues.title: Nine names hammered inside the clasps
clues.description: Condensation reveals the old faculty names on the bands and rehearsal slates record what a later Asking loses when each one is committed.
clues.discovery: Breathe on the iron, inspect the clasp marks, or read Hew’s partial-rite rehearsal notes.

clues.title: A scullion’s story of the bell that cost nothing
clues.description: During a maintenance accident one vault bell sounded, but Caddoc reported no lost silence because no name comb touched the spring.
clues.discovery: Question senior kitchen staff about the night the lower bell rang or find the repair meal entry in Nessa’s ledger.

clues.title: The voices distinguish opening from commitment
clues.description: At a band bell the masks order verification and machinery control; only the later water-breath changes their command to irreversible ritual breach.
clues.discovery: Trigger or simulate an arrest bell and compare the command sequence to a committed-channel record.

clues.title: The finger-wide arrest notch
clues.description: Every clasp stops visibly before the combing stroke, and the engraved instruction says to reseat the band if names or witnesses are disputed.
clues.discovery: Inspect a clasp, turn a key cautiously, or read the keeper’s plate below the arrest bells.

clues.title: The lifting ledger counts four floor dogs and nine bands separately
clues.description: Roof crews are instructed to confirm four released travel dogs before taking load, while the nine ritual bands must remain seated throughout a lift.
clues.discovery: Read the windlass ledger or inspect the old lift diagram beside the counterweight cage.

clues.title: Keeping tubes lead to four travel levers
clues.description: The final declaration operates four bronze lines labeled by route and custody rather than any of the nine funerary faculties.
clues.discovery: Trace the Keeping tubes behind the lower landing or operate a complete custody declaration.

clues.title: The four dogs beneath the living-oak runners
clues.description: Four square floor bolts secure the cradle independently of the nine iron bands; each has a lever line, service key, and removable shear pin.
clues.discovery: Inspect beneath the cradle, test the keeper’s tree, or compare the service tools to the ritual keys.

clues.title: Centuries of Askings without nine centuries of depletion
clues.description: The chapel register records repeated lawful Askings while the same nine silences remain, noting loss only when a dead guest was coerced or prevented from departing.
clues.discovery: Compare the long rite register to the dates of communal silence observances.

clues.title: The founder’s account calls the silences lent, not paid
clues.description: The first custody covenant says the dead borrows the hush of the living and returns it upon taking leave, distinguishing hospitality from expenditure.
clues.discovery: Read the founder’s account beside the original Compact or ask Aderyn about the old wording.

clues.title: The Band of Rest feeds every return channel
clues.description: When Rest is seated, nine narrow grooves carry settling water back beneath the other bands; Mael’s Muster wedges those return grooves open to prevent recovery.
clues.discovery: Inspect the lowest band and spring channels or compare proper and Muster fittings.

clues.title: Jurists demand the three wet leaves
clues.description: The skeptical nobles say they will recognize a Full Asking only if claimant, keeper, and contrary copies emerge from the vault with unbroken band marks.
clues.discovery: Listen to the legal dispute after Mael’s declaration or question a household jurist about admissible dead testimony.

clues.title: The witness rubric forbids a single official digest
clues.description: Caddoc’s procedure places unwaxed vellum on three opposed benches so exact speech is preserved before any faction summarizes it.
clues.discovery: Read the witness instructions or examine the prepared blank leaves in the chapel chest.

clues.title: Black-water grooves in three benches
clues.description: The claimant, keeper, and contrary benches each carry a channel that writes the exchange and stamps the marks of every band present.
clues.discovery: Inspect the witness steps or wet a blank leaf while the spring is settled.

clues.title: Resin for the maintenance combs
clues.description: Kitchen stores supply the clear pine resin used to protect spare comb teeth; an uncleansed duplicate cannot carry scratched names into the spring.
clues.discovery: Check the maintenance caddy, question a cooper, or obtain Nessa’s help preparing a convincing duplicate.

clues.title: Trial failures produce verification rather than counsel
clues.description: The command ledger distinguishes jammed keys, blank water, wrong-band combs, and contested questions, each buying a different interval before Mael can recommence.
clues.discovery: Set two rehearsal faults beside one another or make a mask recite what the House does when band and comb disagree.

clues.title: Four components named on the war table
clues.description: The operating slate requires matching band, comb, spoken names, and question; shallow cuts, filled teeth, wrong keys, or disputed wording halt the process at visible stages.
clues.discovery: Inspect the war table, test a maintenance duplicate, or read Caddoc’s checklist.

clues.title: The nine long penances
clues.description: A restoration litany prescribes restored names, whole histories, just reasons, fulfilled obligations, uncoerced words, anniversaries, honored refusals, answered duties, and rest rather than smithwork.
clues.discovery: Read the forbidden restoration leaf or ask Caddoc what followed the oldest recorded diminishment.

clues.title: Reforged iron beside an empty faculty
clues.description: A household account pays for a replaced band within a month but records that the missing Reply did not return until three generations completed the dead woman’s unanswered charge.
clues.discovery: Compare the smith’s invoice to the later memorial accounts in Aderyn’s archive.

clues.title: New metal over an old dry channel
clues.description: One clasp is visibly younger than its band, yet the restoration marks continue for decades afterward, proving physical repair did not restore sacred capacity.
clues.discovery: Inspect the repaired clasp and follow its dated marks into the witness register.

clues.title: Caddoc’s hidden Night of Hearing rubric
clues.description: The old chapel copy permits a witness, founder authority, and military surety to seat the bands and suspend every use until dawn when custody itself is disputed.
clues.discovery: Lift Mael’s pasted emergency amendment or persuade Caddoc to disclose the omitted provision.

clues.title: The founder seal beside three empty names
clues.description: The original Compact leaves spaces for chapel witness, founder’s house, and living-defense surety and explicitly postpones ownership until after the hearing.
clues.discovery: Break the linen tie on the original Compact or ask Aderyn why the seal was cut with three witness notches.

clues.title: Three joined keyholes on the keeper’s tree
clues.description: A chapel key, founder key, and military key turned together seat every arrest and transfer the cradle dogs to joint custody until dawn.
clues.discovery: Set the old three-key keeper lock beside Mael’s single override and follow which dogs each can command.

clues.title: Nine hearths on Sib’s tide book
clues.description: A carrying-road mark inside Sib’s tide book shows nine hearths passing one vessel in a circuit; Gwyne identifies three surviving keeper lines and a disputed Mere House claim.
clues.discovery: Examine the tide book or ask Gwyne who may contest the destination.

clues.title: The interrupted carrying calendar
clues.description: The chapel calendar records nine winter custodians and fifty-three years of Taran emergency renewals without final release from surviving hearths.
clues.discovery: Open the memorial chest or persuade Caddoc to explain pre-Taran custody.

clues.title: Tomas’s nine-loop cord
clues.description: Tomas presents a Mere House token and green cord tied in nine unequal loops, naming Mother Eluned and the surviving Trust.
clues.discovery: Demand Tomas name his patron at the keeper’s stone.

clues.title: Six marks on the capstan table
clues.description: The service-rise table counts complete cauldron and cradle as six ordinary burden marks before bearers, evidence, or tools.
clues.discovery: Read the cooper’s chalk loads or test the platform.

clues.title: The windlass and punt agree
clues.description: The lifting ledger assigns six marks to the cradle and notes that the carrying punt has only three remaining dry marks.
clues.discovery: Compare the roof lift book to the old boat diagram.

clues.title: Nine dry marks on the punt
clues.description: Draft marks show the cradle takes six of nine safe loads, while two boat hands and one keeper occupy the remainder.
clues.discovery: Read the draft marks or load the crossbeam.

clues.title: Correction leaves after seizures
clues.description: Historical corrections show victors and porters holding the cradle while the prior keeper remained recorded until witnessed transfer.
clues.discovery: Open the Keeping panels and compare possession to correction.

clues.title: The keeper’s name remains after release
clues.description: Releasing all four custody dogs changes mobility but leaves keeper, destination, and authority visible in black water.
clues.discovery: Release a dog while watching the keeper’s tree.

clues.title: The third handprint refuses a seizure
clues.description: Taking a tow line or surrounding the boat does not wake the receiving and witness prints; the previous keeper remains.
clues.discovery: Test the keeper’s stone during a contested handoff.

clues.title: The sacred-object recovery articles
clues.description: Vane’s posted articles forbid arrows, fire, hooks, and mounted pursuit around sacred water and direct guards to seize routes and bearers alive.
clues.discovery: Read the gate sergeant’s standing articles.

clues.title: The red recovery strip
clues.description: The command strip reads: hold the route, take the bearers living, preserve the water, and do not strike the cradle.
clues.discovery: Lift the red shutter strip or make a mask recite it.

clues.title: Wheel chocks instead of arrow slits
clues.description: The post has runner chocks, rope knives, shields, and braces but no firing slit aimed at the cauldron channel.
clues.discovery: Search the post or observe the first response.

clues.title: The chapel’s testimony rubric
clues.description: The rubric says one complete black-water leaf and two named witnesses stay an oath founded on a contrary recital until hearing.
clues.discovery: Read Caddoc’s witness-leaf rules.

clues.title: Aderyn’s contradiction clause
clues.description: The founding oath forbids renewal over authenticated royal testimony and requires delay until noon.
clues.discovery: Unseal Aderyn’s contradiction clause and trace the noon delay into the founder’s oath.

clues.title: Waterproof witness tubes
clues.description: Three reed-and-wax tubes are prepared for leaves, with instructions to send any surviving copy and two witnesses to the herald.
clues.discovery: Search the waiting punt or question its boatman.

clues.title: The cooper’s service-rise plan
clues.description: The east rise lifts the cradle to a disguised cooper’s cart, trading speed for staff-yard movement and witnesses.
clues.discovery: Inspect the platform or ask Nessa what can leave.

clues.title: The two-stage roof extraction
clues.description: The north windlass raises the cradle and the siege crane lowers it outside, offering fast movement that the whole court can witness.
clues.discovery: Trace the lift cable or read the crane diagram.

clues.title: Three route wheels
clues.description: North, east, and southwest wheels send the target toward exposed roof, disguised kitchens, or fast private weir.
clues.discovery: Inspect the keeper’s tree or runner channels.

clues.title: The clerks’ reduced memorial columns
clues.description: Before the rolls are chained, clerks recopy each dead person as office, campaign, and useful answer. Spouses, sworn promises, causes defended, and recorded refusals remain on the household originals but vanish from Mael’s war register.
clues.discovery: Compare a household memorial roll with the shortened entry fastened into the central register.

clues.title: The rejected petition’s first question
clues.description: The retained petition gives the exact first question, names three opposed witnesses, and promises that Branoc’s whole answer will be copied before any claimant argues from it.
clues.discovery: Read the petition copy filed beside Mael’s refusal at the heralds’ bench.

clues.title: The herald’s Night of Hearing rubric
clues.description: A marginal rubric directs the presiding herald to suspend use of the cauldron until dawn when chapel witness, founder authority, and military surety jointly dispute an Asking or transfer.
clues.discovery: Inspect the renewal copy Nia keeps open beneath the speaking order.

clues.title: Two correct orders on one bell slate
clues.description: One underkeep order commands the east passage cleared to protect the grain route; another commands it sealed to deny an intruder. Both bear valid voice colors and the same minute mark, so the kitchen staff waited for a living officer.
clues.discovery: Compare the paired orders still clipped beside the third-bell board.

clues.title: The oath book’s sunrise latch
clues.description: The chapel oath book remains physically unlatched until sunrise. Its renewal leaf cannot receive seals before the memorial answer is read, and a stayed testimony leaf keeps the latch shut until noon.
clues.discovery: Examine the brass sunrise latch on the open Compact register.

clues.title: The disputed-name reseating rule
clues.description: The keeper’s register orders a raised band reseated whenever a name, witness, or question is challenged before the matching comb touches water. Several old entries record bells sounded and no silence lost.
clues.discovery: Read the red-ink corrections beside earlier disputed Askings.

clues.title: Aderyn’s nine-part founder diagram
clues.description: A founder’s diagram labels the nine bands with face, road, measure, hearth, hand, season, bar, reply, and rest, then warns that an Asking lacking any one returns a diminished person rather than a smaller quantity of power.
clues.discovery: Unroll the narrow vellum stored with the founder’s seal case.

clues.title: The leaf no household could abridge
clues.description: An old black-water leaf preserves the invited dead woman’s answer, the claimant’s interruption, the keeper’s correction, and the contrary witness’s objection in one continuous script. A later summary omits two lines, but the leaf makes the omission obvious.
clues.discovery: Compare the sealed witness leaf with the household abstract filed beside it.

clues.title: The founder’s circuit account
clues.description: A household account records no sale or permanent gift to House Taran. It lists nine receiving hearths, nine departure witnesses, and Dunwarren’s turn as one custody season in a repeating circuit.
clues.discovery: Read the oldest account tied beneath Aderyn’s replacement covenant.

clues.title: The four absences in a failed declaration
clues.description: A rejected stair record names the dead and states a question but leaves the anchor, willing witnesses, dead person’s freedom to refuse, and living keeper unstated. The door records the words exactly and does not open.
clues.discovery: Read the oldest incomplete declaration preserved across the three landings.

clues.title: The Name landing recognizes Branoc’s ring
clues.description: When Branoc’s whole name is spoken beside the oath-ring, the Name landing produces a fresh royal handprint where two centuries of copied seals and relic claims left no mark.
clues.discovery: Present or closely test the ring at the Landing of Name.

clues.title: Edric’s recital remains a witness statement
clues.description: A centuries-old declaration repeats the Compact’s sentence as “Branoc’s command,” but the stair preserves the speaker’s source as Edric Taran’s recital and never marks the words as Branoc’s own answer.
clues.discovery: Compare the compact formula with the source line cut beneath it at the Landing of Asking.

clues.title: The council obeys the declared noun
clues.description: Two rehearsal transcripts differ only in whether the keeper declared “the vale” or “Dunwarren.” The borrowed council redirects every answer accordingly and never corrects the narrower wording from apparent intent.
clues.discovery: Compare the paired transcripts pinned below the command table.

clues.title: The fifth-bell commitment rack
clues.description: Nine band keys, nine full-depth combs, the chained memorial register, and a fifth-bell water order have been staged together. Unlike the earlier needles, every comb reaches the commitment stroke.
clues.discovery: Inspect the prepared Muster rack beside the question board.

clues.title: The command retracted in its owner’s hand
clues.description: One return channel carries a black-water correction in Captain Alwen Reed’s hand: after her whole name and the civilians behind her delaying action were restored, the retained order changed from “hold” to “withdraw them first” and then ceased.
clues.discovery: Open the capped return channel beneath Alwen Reed’s speaking line.

clues.title: Only the whole cradle fits the carrying road
clues.description: The brake, burden marks, and receiving grooves align with the living-oak runners and all nine relational bands. The bronze vessel alone cannot engage the old road or preserve the returning water paths.
clues.discovery: Compare the worn runner grooves with the cauldron’s separate bronze feet.

clues.title: Nine receiving cuts require a keeper’s hand
clues.description: Each historic receiving cut pairs a hearth mark with a living handprint, named destination, and authority for the next Asking. Untended arrivals stop above the tide line even when the runners and grate are clear.
clues.discovery: Read the keeper cuts along the inner carrying threshold.

clues.title: Nine wet return lines after one departure
clues.description: An old receiving stone records one honored dead person’s willing departure with all nine return channels wet and every band mark present on the next hearth’s acceptance cut.
clues.discovery: Wash the silt from the oldest complete departure-and-receipt record.
